issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency: The problem statement and template expect concrete animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (UML and template Main create Seal, Pig, Goat). The solution repository instead provides classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SpaceSeal.java, SpacePig.java, SpaceGoat.java) and leaves Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java empty. This mismatch between expected class names (Seal, Pig, Goat) and the actual solution classes (SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat) will prevent students from compiling or running the provided template Main and will confuse readers of the problem because the class identifiers referenced in the UML/template do not exist in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the concrete class identifiers in the solution match the problem/template. Options: (a) Rename SpaceSeal -> Seal, SpacePig -> Pig, SpaceGoat -> Goat (keep implementations identical), or (b) implement Seal, Pig, Goat classes that extend/delegate to the existing Space* classes (for example, `public class Seal extends SpaceSeal { public Seal(String name){ super(name); } }`) and remove or populate the currently empty Seal.java, Pig.java, Goat.java files. Ensure these classes are in package de.tum.cit.ase and implement the interfaces and method behavior specified in the UML (Seal: Rideable & Milkable, Pig: Rideable, Goat: Milkable) so the template Main and tests compile and run as described.

issues.description: Concept: the concrete animal classes used in the exercise (the three animal types students are asked to implement/instantiate). Problem statement and template expect classes named 'Seal', 'Pig', and 'Goat' (e.g., UML and example code use Seal, Pig, Goat). Solution repository instead provides classes named 'SpaceSeal', 'SpacePig', and 'SpaceGoat'. This is an identifier naming mismatch: the same conceptual entities (seal, pig, goat) are represented with different class names across artifacts. A student reading the problem and template will look for/implement Seal, Pig, Goat, but the solution reference uses SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat, which breaks a direct name-to-concept mapping and increases cognitive load (students may think these are different or wonder whether additional adapter classes are required). This can block automated checks or confuse reconciliation between student's code and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make names consistent for the same conceptual entities. Options: (A) Rename the solution classes to Seal, Pig, and Goat (update class declarations and filenames accordingly) so they match the problem statement and template; (B) Update the problem statement and template to refer to SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat everywhere; or (C) Add thin adapter classes Seal, Pig, Goat in the solution that delegate to SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat (e.g., public class Seal extends SpaceSeal { public Seal(String n){ super(n);} }) so the expected names exist while preserving the existing Space* implementations.
